[WP] Tell me the Legend of the Voat Goat.

The Alien and The Goat

The Alien was a popular being, with both animals and humans envying and admiring his unique abilities. He came from far away, with much knowledge of technology and the universe. The Alien was known around the village, but unforunately his power started to get to him.

He started to mock others just for having opposing viewpoints. He silenced those easily because he was intimidating. Every time others tried to voice their opinion on his arrogance, they were silenced by his special alien abilities.

One day, the Goat, a commoner in the village, was eating grass, minding his own business. He was passing out flyers for a group he just started, while simultaneously eating grass.

The Alien mocked it, laughing loudly as he walked by.

"You're just a goat! Nobody will come to your stupid meetings."

The Goat was saddened, but continued on his way.

On the first meeting, only a rabbit and a turtle showed up. He was happy with that though, and they had some great discussions.

Each week, the numbers slowly grew.

The Alien obviously started to worry, so he mocked louder and harder. He silenced any who tried to defend the poor goat.

Eventually at one of the meetings, the topic of The Alien came up.

Members wanted to hurt The Alien in the way they were hurt by him, but the Goat made a very noble point.

"The best way to fight the Alien is to do what we are doing. Let's continue these meetings and grow in numbers."

The Alien started to notice he was ignored more often. He tried harder and harder to get attention, but as the Goat's community grew, it was getting more difficult for him.

In the end, The Alien decided it did not need the community anymore, and he stayed in his own place, with a few who still supported and worshipped his bullying tactics.

As for the Goat, he founded Voat, a community for members to discuss various topics in an uncensored but friendly environment.

Moral: A community coming together peacefully often is stronger than they think.
